tei:div.tei:p:
I hasten for aid and find God near me at the time when I call with my voice. In the congregation of God, He stands in my midst and here in this miniature sanctuary I mutter to Him with my voice. Test me, examine me, a stray sheep am I, I have been cast off and silenced so that I cannot raise my voice. When my shearers say ‘she is rejected’, her guardian and protector does not roar with His voice. When I conversed of His statutes and my sound was pleasing, He inclined His ear and spoke; ‘Let me hear the sound of your voice’. Swiftly He fled from me like the deer on the rocky mountains, when He desired law and a sign from me and in my dwellings there was no voice. He who leapt from fragment to fragment (Abraham), let him restore Him to me, perhaps He will raise your face because you heard His voice. Plead on their behalf, behold the sheep on Moriah, let his silent submission (Isaac) justify those who did not listen to His voice. Keep far from the smooth one (Jacob) the hairy
hands (of Esau), when he meditates on entreaties, for to Thee is his voice. Grant help that the testimony should not be forgotten and from the mouth of His seed there should be no end to his voice. My seers and my spokesmen, the sons of my mother, remonstrated with me that I should hear Thy voice. They stand on their watch and cry out; let the secret be revealed to them that the Lord may answer them with His voice. He has left me, I wander about and seek Him, He is in every place, where shall I raise my voice? The fame of my Beloved is below, He is mighty on high, ‘the whole earth is full of His glory’ do they call out above with their voice. The soldiers in the waters through which He made a path (the Sea of Reeds) said ‘we have seen no form but only a voice’. I searched for Him in the desert and they said that He is not there, yet when of old He gave His law, He frightened me with His voice. In purity He leapt over mountains and paths and from His dwelling on Mount Moriah He once sent forth His voice. When I defiled His dear dwelling, He rose up from it, on the hidden day there will come in my ears a voice. I was dear in His eyes and He adhered to me
in captivity, ‘I am with him’ He assured me then with His voice. He went down to Shinear and set up His throne in Elam, where He made heard like a lion and like a serpent a voice. He saved me from the bear — when the work from the Sanctuary was disturbed — which had been inscribed in writing and proclaimed by a voice. He subdued for me the four heads of the leopard and in my gratitude I make heard to Him my voice. He then sold the land to the wild beast of the reeds, ‘who is above me in heaven?’ it boasted aloud with its voice. To the God of my salvation from the teeth of iron I cried and from before the trampling foot I shrieked with my voice. He has not made known to me the measure of my end, when in my land the turtle dove will make heard its voice. Even from scholars has He concealed my end, that my seers may not know the time when they will lift up their voice. Pray look and see my woe and my pain, there is no friend to me to whom I can raise my voice. For ever shall I hope that no word shall be omitted from those who listen for a still small voice. In my midst my heart rejoices when I hear my Beloved sounding on my doors with His voice.
Truly He will bear me as a seal on the heart as once when beneath the apple tree He roused me with His voice. As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘And it happened on the third day during the morning that there was thunder and lightning and a heavy cloud lay over the mountain and there was a very powerful sound of the Shofar and all the people in the camp were afraid’. Thou hast raised me, O God, over all daughters since on my behalf on Horeb didst Thou give voice. Over all gods art Thou greatly exalted, to eternity shalt Thou be exalted with the Teruah’s voice. As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘God has arisen with Teruah, the Lord with a Shofar sound’. And it is said: ‘With trumpets and a Shofar sound cry out before the King, the Lord’. A bird from Egypt (Israel) cooed from the wilderness and a dove from Assyria sounded its voice. Take note of the bird of Thy household, seek out the patient dove, blow the Shofar for them and whistle to them with Thy voice.
As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem’. Fasten Thy laws to me lest they fly away like the eagle, lest there take flight those who make heard Thy voice. I will learn the pure law with my eyes on my Teacher just as once His messenger (Moses) spoke and God answered him with His voice. As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘And the sound of the Shofar grew very powerful, Moses was speaking and God was answering him aloud’. The end has approached, the time of judgment comes, a defender arises to entreat with his voice. The new moon is sanctified and the feast prepared, so let me blow the Shofar that He may answer me with His voice. As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘Blow the Shofar on the new moon, when the moon is covered on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob’.
There will be stirring from the grave, a shout from the rock when the dry bones from the dust give voice. Witness the banner on the mountains and the sound of the Shofar on earth when there is heard the exultation of those long silent of voice. As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘All inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, when the banner is raised on the mountains shall you see and when the Shofar is blown shall you hear’. No longer shall the heart mocked by error refuse to incline, no longer shall the ear be deaf and not hear the voice. Restore to me as of old the law of my inheritance, as when Thou didst shatter me with lightning and the voice. As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘And all the people were seeing the thunder and the lightning and the sound of the Shofar and the mountain in smoke, the people saw and trembled and stood at a distance.stood at a distance’. Wisdom was uttered by one wise in words (David) who composed the pleasantest of songs with pleasantness of
voice. He taught all to give praise to God who rules over all, that they might know how to sweeten their voice. As it is written in Thy holy words: Halleluyah, praise God in His sanctuary, praise Him in His strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar’s blast, praise Him with zither and harp. Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him on string instruments and flute, praise Him with the clash of cymbals, praise Him with the ring of cymbals. Let all with breath praise the Lord, Halleluyah. Instead of the sons of Zion the sons of Yavan were laid low, Thou didst make Thy arrows flash and confound them with a voice. Thunder against my plunderers, blow with the Shofar, in the whirlwinds of the south let there go forth a voice. As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them’.
